definition: Amália is a Portuguese large language model (LLM) announced in November 2024 by the Portuguese Prime-Minister Luís Montenegro.
details: Its final version is expected to be launched in 2026. It is being developed by Center for Responsible AI (Centro para a AI Responsável) and by the research centers of NOVA School of Science and Technology and Instituto Superior Técnico.

explainer.lead: Amália is a large language model being built in Portugal with a focus on European Portuguese, Portuguese culture and data protection. Announced in November 2024, it is intended for use in public administration and is expected to become an open model in its final 2026 release.

tiers.eli5: Amália is a computer program being taught to understand and write the kind of Portuguese spoken in Portugal. It is a bit like building a helpful library assistant who knows the local language and customs, rather than speaking a more general version of Portuguese. People working for Portugal's public administration received a test version in 2025, while the finished version is expected in 2026.
tiers.practitioner: The immediate application is Portuguese Public Administration, whose users received exclusive access to the September 2025 beta. Engineering plans should account for its European Portuguese focus and its stated priorities of cultural representation and data protection. The final release is expected in 2026 and is described as an open model, but the beta's administrative restriction limits general experimentation.
tiers.paperLevel: Amália is an LLM designed around three stated objectives: the European Portuguese linguistic variant, cultural representation and data protection. Its development involves the Center for Responsible AI and research centers at NOVA School of Science and Technology and Instituto Superior Técnico. A September 2025 beta was restricted to Public Administration, with an open final model expected in 2026.

explainer.example: During the September 2025 beta, an employee of Portuguese Public Administration could use Amália within that restricted rollout. Someone outside Public Administration could not access that beta and would have to wait for a wider release.

usedIn.name: Portuguese Public Administration
usedIn.detail: The Portuguese Agency for Administrative Modernization announced its adoption in 2024, and the September 2025 beta was available only to Public Administration.

flow: The development partners build Amália around European Portuguese, cultural representation and data protection.
The project entered beta in 2025, with the September beta restricted to Public Administration.
The final version is expected in 2026 and is intended to be an open model.
explainer.origin: Portuguese Prime Minister Luís Montenegro announced Amália in November 2024. It is being developed by the Center for Responsible AI and research centers at NOVA School of Science and Technology and Instituto Superior Técnico.
explainer.lineage: Amália progressed from its November 2024 announcement to a beta phase announced in April 2025 and released to Public Administration in September. Its next planned stage is the open final version expected in 2026.
explainer.whyItMatters: The project treats European Portuguese and Portuguese cultural representation as explicit goals rather than assuming that a general Portuguese model is sufficient. Its public-administration rollout also makes data protection a central design priority.
